moat_against: Commodity product, no pricing power — deposits and loans are fungible; NIM is earned through repricing/mix, not owned, and deposit repricing is outside management control
Credit-cycle exposure — NPAs rose in Q2 2026 (CRE, agriculture, consumer goods); net charge-offs 42 bps; provisions are the swing factor in any downturn
Capital-constrained — loan growth, the dividend and the buyback compete for the same CET1; Basel III endgame still evolving
Scale/efficiency disadvantage vs money-center banks; ~$1B of guided technology investment just to keep pace
Scotiabank dilution to re-earn — diluted shares 949.6M (FY2024) to 1,108.0M (FY2025); the buyback must retire that before per-share compounding restarts
moat_for: Deposit/relationship franchise at scale — 16 states, Ohio/New York/Washington largest deposit markets; average C&I loans up 11.7% YoY in Q2 2026
Diversified fee engines — investment banking and debt placement, cards/payments, trust/wealth (record AUM), commercial mortgage servicing
NIM rebuild printing — 2.89% in Q2 2026 (+23 bps YoY), ~$9B fixed-rate assets repricing H2 2026 and ~$21B in 2027, deposit costs down 36 bps YoY
Capital bolstered — Scotiabank ~$2.8B strategic stake, CET1 11.2% at Q2 2026, $341M repurchased in Q2 2026 with at least $1.3B expected for 2026
moat_justification: Weak-to-moderate regional-bank franchise: a real deposit and relationship franchise across 16 states (Ohio, New York, Washington the largest deposit markets) with genuine fee engines (investment banking/debt placement, payments, trust/wealth, commercial mortgage servicing), a NIM rebuild actually printing (2.89% in Q2 2026, +23 bps YoY, guided 3.00-3.05% in 2026 and 3.25%+ in 2027) and capital bolstered by Scotiabank's ~$2.8B strategic minority investment (CET1 11.2% at Q2 2026, buybacks resumed) — against a commodity banking product with no structural pricing power (the NIM is earned through repricing and mix, not owned), full credit-cycle exposure (NPAs rising in CRE/agriculture/consumer; net charge-offs 42 bps), capital-constrained growth and capital return, money-center scale disadvantage, and per-share dilution from the Scotiabank issuance (diluted shares 949.6M in FY2024 to 1,108.0M in FY2025) that the resumed buyback must first retire. ROTCE >15% by 2027 is guided, not proven through a cycle. A 4 gives CAP 7.2 years.
name: KeyCorp
one_liner: Improving super-regional bank, moat 4/10 — median OE $1.78/sh is an 8.92% yield at $19.92, but on through-cycle starts the weighted IRR is 11.85% (IV@15% $14.85) and even the bull case only reaches ~$19.77, so it clears 15% only below ~$14.85; bank-model mismatch, confidence low.
